clusters.mechanism: EvalRunner.resume re-validates the stored request against the current catalog, so a removed model ID is rejected (HTTP 400) and legacy evals cannot resume. The new test asserts this rejection.

manageLocal builds new URL(`http://${host}:8080`) from an unvalidated remote_host with no error handling. Valid SSH destinations such as bare IPv6 addresses or host:port values make it throw TypeError: Invalid URL and abort the command.

The remote provider is matched only by exact origin equality between http://<remote_host>:8080 and the provider's base_url. An SSH alias, user@host or https therefore matches nothing, so the probe runs without the API key and enablement is never toggled.
RuntimePolicy strictly validates persisted routing cells and provider preferences at construction, so retired provider or model IDs saved by an operator stop the daemon from starting.
The removed-models tests depend on the absent evals/triage/cases.json dataset. They fail with ENOENT before reaching the resume validation they are meant to exercise.
The LAN provider test does not cover mapping the removed built-in's Claude-harness base_url onto a config-defined provider (agentic path). This is a test coverage gap.
The OPERATIONS.md link uses the anchor GUIDE.md#providers-1, which points to the second 'Providers' heading instead of the first, where the LAN example lives.

The docs still describe the llama-server binary at ~/.local/share/limitless/llama-bin/, but the generated unit now defaults to /usr/local/bin/llama-server, so the default points to a nonexistent binary on the documented setup.
